how: cd e2e && npx lhci autorun --config=lighthouserc.json, twice: 3 runs per URL each, 6 in all
why: JSON carries no comments, so the provenance for every threshold in `ci`
lives here as data instead -- and a test reads it. `worst` is the worst
value observed across every run for that URL: the largest for a
maxNumericValue budget, the smallest for a minScore one. Every threshold
in `ci.assert` must have an entry here that it clears, which is what
makes it a MEASURED budget rather than an aspirational one.
enforces that pairing, so a threshold cannot be added without a
measurement and cannot be relaxed past the number it was derived from.
BUILD THE SITE WITH --base-url MATCHING THE ORIGIN IT IS SERVED FROM.
Zola bakes absolute config.base_url URLs into every page, and base.html's
own `default-src 'self'` then blocks all of them as cross-origin. The
resulting page has no CSS, no script and no images -- and scores 100 on
performance with a 0.000 layout shift. That is not a hypothetical: it is
what the first collection run on this repository produced, on all five
URLs, before anyone asked why a 19 MB site was loading in 473 ms.
Both quality.yml jobs assert the built HTML links its own origin before
knownDefects: Every page is budgeted at 0.02 CLS and measures 0 in all six runs. Until
2026-09-17 /download/ carried a 0.15 ceiling on a shift nobody had
explained; it was two mechanisms, both fixed that day. The
platform-detection banner painted empty and was filled after an async
client-hint call (e2e/tests/download-layout.spec.js), and the web fonts
loaded from fonts.bunny.net with display=swap re-wrapped text when they
arrived (e2e/tests/web-fonts.spec.js). /download/ went from 0.105-0.150
on CI to 0.062-0.065 after the first fix, and to 0 locally after the second.
SEO is capped at 0.92 site-wide by the `robots-txt` audit, which rejects
the `Content-Signal:` line in website/static/robots.txt as an unknown
directive. The directive is deliberate; Lighthouse does not know it. The
seo budget is 0.90 for that reason and not because 0.92 is the goal.
The site under measurement is a ZOLA-ONLY build. Two assets that the
Pages deploy adds afterwards are therefore missing, and both 404 during
collection (six of six runs each on 2026-09-17): /analyze/ requests /wasm/sipnab_bg.wasm,
which pages.yml creates with wasm-pack, and /docs/ requests
/pagefind/pagefind.js, which pages.yml creates with the pagefind binary.
Both 404s were present when the numbers below were taken, so the 0.96
best-practices scores already account for them. If the docs pages start
scoring under the 0.95 best-practices floor, the fix is
to run the same pagefind index step these two jobs' sibling `docs` job
already runs, so the measured artifact matches the deployed one -- not to
lower the floor.
`uses-text-compression` scores 0 and `uses-long-cache-ttl` scores 0.5 in
every run. Both are properties of `python3 -m http.server`, which sends
neither gzip nor Cache-Control; GitHub Pages sends both. They are left
switched ON rather than disabled, because the category scores below were
measured with them failing -- the budget already accounts for them, and
disabling an audit is how a gate quietly stops covering something.
